pieces.passage: One always travels to a place by the sea, but last year he decided to travel to an island. Knowing that it was cold and rainy, he found the weather colder and rainier than expected. He did not see the sun and the rain continued for nine continuous days. A tour guide taught them how to keep their things dry and safe. During the last four days, the weather became sunny and pleasant, and they enjoyed the beach.

pieces.passage:
Many people think globalization is a new phenomenon. In fact, this process has been happening for thousands of years. For example, some very old Chinese artifacts have been found in North and South America, and antique Arabian money has been found as far north as Norway.

What is even more remarkable is how quickly plants from the New World became staples in the Old World. Hungarian cooking is famous for red peppers, and the Irish are famous for eating potatoes. Indian food is an even better example. In many “traditional” Indian dishes, you may find potatoes, tomatoes, squash, corn, sweet peppers, peanuts, cashew nuts, guavas, or papaya.

We think of all this food as traditional Indian food. Yet sailors brought these plants to India from America on ships after 1500. They took a long time to spread and become popular. The chili pepper is now part of diets from South Africa to China, but it originated in the Americas. Globalization is really nothing new; it has happened since people began to trade.
